title: What can you say about evening primrose oil in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 1 wording for evening primrose oil; the strongest is "Provides omega-6 fatty acids, including linoleic acid, for the maintenance of good health" (moderate, 1.3-6 g a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats eczema (atopic dermatitis)".

supported_wordings.wording: Provides omega-6 fatty acids, including linoleic acid, for the maintenance of good health.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 1.3-6 g a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 1.3-6 g of evening primrose oil a day.

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Evening Primrose Oil

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Relieves breast pain (mastalgia) or PMS symptoms
Ripens the cervix or brings on labor
wordings_to_avoid.why: Describes a drug action in pregnancy.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
